items.title: Fooled twice: People cannot detect deepfakes but think they can

judge.reason: O artigo aborda a detecção de deepfakes por humanos (tópico certo), é um estudo empírico com experimento comportamental, o método descrito bate com o resumo, e o achado principal é totalmente suportado pelo resumo.

items.title: Deepfake detection by human crowds, machines, and machine-informed crowds

judge.evidence_empirical: In two online studies with 15,016 participants, we present authentic videos and deepfakes and ask participants to identify which is which.
judge.evidence_topic: The recent emergence of deepfake videos raises theoretical and practical questions. Are humans or the leading machine learning model more capable of detecting algorithmic visual manipulations of videos?
judge.reason: O artigo aborda a detecção humana de deepfakes em vídeos, atende ao recorte de estudos empíricos com participantes humanos, o método descrito coincide com o resumo e o achado principal é integralmente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: AI-synthesized faces are indistinguishable from real faces and more trustworthy

judge.evidence_empirical: O resumo não menciona participantes humanos; afirma apenas: 'Our evaluation of the photorealism of AI-synthesized faces indicates that synthesis engines have passed through the uncanny valley and are capable of creating faces that are indistinguishable-and more trustworthy-than real faces.'
judge.evidence_topic: O resumo trata da avaliação do fotorrealismo de rostos sintetizados por IA e de sua credibilidade percebida, abordando diretamente como pessoas percebem e julgam a credibilidade de imagens sintéticas.
judge.reason: O artigo não atende ao pedido porque o resumo não descreve um estudo empírico com participantes humanos, exigido pelas restrições. Apenas menciona uma 'avaliação do fotorrealismo' sem especificar coleta de dados com seres humanos.

items.title: AI Hyperrealism: Why AI Faces Are Perceived as More Real Than Human Ones

judge.evidence_empirical: In Experiment 1 (N = 124 adults), alongside our reanalysis of previously published data, we showed that White AI faces are judged as human more often than actual human faces... In Experiment 2 (N = 610 adults), we used face-space theory and participant qualitative reports...
judge.evidence_topic: White AI faces are judged as human more often than actual human faces—a phenomenon we term AI hyperrealism.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga como humanos percebem rostos gerados por IA, alinhado ao pedido. Apresenta dois experimentos com participantes humanos (N=124 e N=610), configurando estudo empírico experimental. O método extraído condiz com o resumo. O achado principal está claramente declarado no resumo: rostos de IA brancos são julgados como humanos com mais frequência do que rostos reais.

items.title: AI-generated images of familiar faces are indistinguishable from real photographs

judge.evidence_empirical: Our results demonstrated that generated images of both fictional (Experiment 1) and celebrity identities (Experiment 2) could not be distinguished from real photographs.
judge.evidence_topic: Human users are now able to generate synthetic face images with artificial intelligence (AI) tools. Although indistinguishable from real photographs...
judge.reason: O artigo investiga a detecção humana de imagens sintéticas de rostos geradas por IA, tema central do pedido. É um estudo empírico experimental. O método extraído (quatro experimentos) confere com o resumo. O achado principal está integralmente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Training human super-recognizers' detection and discrimination of AI-generated faces

judge.evidence_empirical: we investigate synthetic face detection and discrimination in super-recognizers (SRs; who have exceptional face recognition skills), and typical-ability control participants. We also devised a training procedure which sought to highlight rendering artefacts. In two different experimental designs, we found that SRs (total N = 283) were better at detecting and discriminating synthetic faces than controls (total N = 381)
judge.evidence_topic: The synthetic faces produced by GANs are difficult to detect and are often judged to be more realistic than real faces.
judge.reason: O artigo trata da detecção e discriminação de rostos sintéticos gerados por IA, enquadrando-se no tema do pedido. É um estudo empírico com participantes humanos (experimentos com super-reconhecedores e controles). O método extraído condiz com o resumo. O achado principal está integralmente respaldado pelo trecho do resumo.

items.title: Providing detection strategies to improve human detection of deepfakes: An experimental study

judge.evidence_empirical: In this preregistered online experiment, participants (N = 454, Mage = 37.19, SDage = 13.25, males = 57.5%) categorize a series of 20 videos as either real or deepfake.
judge.evidence_topic: categorize a series of 20 videos as either real or deepfake
judge.reason: O estudo trata da deteção humana de deepfakes, é um experimento empírico com dados próprios, e o achado principal está totalmente alinhado com o resumo.

items.title: Testing human ability to detect 'deepfake' images of human faces

judge.evidence_empirical: Using an online survey, participants (N = 280) were randomly allocated to one of four groups: a control group, and three assistance interventions. Each participant was shown a sequence of 20 images randomly selected from a pool of 50 deepfake images of human faces and 50 images of real human faces.
judge.evidence_topic: This study aims to assess human ability to identify image deepfakes of human faces
judge.reason: O artigo aborda detecção de deepfakes por humanos, conduziu um estudo empírico com survey online e os achados coincidem com o resumo.

items.title: Deepfake detection with and without content warnings

judge.evidence_empirical: We conduct an experiment to measure people's alertness to and ability to detect a high-quality deepfake among a set of videos.
judge.evidence_topic: The rapid advancement of 'deepfake' video technology-which uses deep learning artificial intelligence algorithms to create fake videos that look real-has given urgency to the question of how policymakers and technology companies should moderate inauthentic content. We conduct an experiment to measure people's alertness to and ability to detect a high-quality deepfake among a set of videos.
judge.reason: O resumo relata um experimento com participantes humanos sobre detecção de deepfake, alinhado com o pedido. O método descrito (experimentos com e sem aviso) corresponde ao resumo, e o achado principal é sustentado pelo trecho 'only 21.6% of respondents correctly identify the deepfake...' que mostra baixa identificação e benefício limitado de avisos.

items.title: Conspiracy thinking and social media use are associated with ability to detect deepfakes

judge.evidence_empirical: Our findings show that humans perform better at recognizing deepfake videos of familiar persons compared to deepfakes of unfamiliar persons. Next, our findings show a positive relationship between time spent on social media and deepfake detection performance, as well as conspiracy thinking and deepfake detection performance.
judge.evidence_topic: The aim of the current study was to investigate the predictors of human performance at recognizing deepfake videos.
judge.reason: O resumo relata explicitamente uma relação positiva entre tempo em redes sociais e pensamento conspiratório com o desempenho na detecção de deepfakes, sustentando integralmente o achado extraído.

items.title: Deepfake smiles matter less—the psychological and neural impact of presumed AI-generated faces

judge.evidence_empirical: Using EEG, we tracked participants’ (N = 30) brain responses to real faces showing positive, neutral, and negative expressions, after being informed that they are either real or fake.
judge.evidence_topic: investigate the impact of the belief that depicted persons are real or deepfakes on psychological and neural measures of human face perception
judge.reason: O artigo trata da percepção de rostos presumidamente gerados por IA, sendo um estudo empírico experimental com EEG. O método extraído corresponde ao resumo, e o achado está exatamente respaldado pela conclusão do resumo.

items.title: Real and Deepfake Face Recognition: An EEG Study on Cognitive and Emotive Implications

judge.evidence_empirical: EEG data were collected from 23 healthy participants using a 21-channel dry-EEG headset; power spectrum and event-related potential (ERP) analyses were performed.
judge.evidence_topic: This study investigated healthy individuals' cognitive and emotional engagement in a visual discrimination task involving real and deepfake human faces expressing positive, negative, or neutral emotions.
judge.reason: O resumo descreve um estudo empírico com participantes humanos, usando EEG para investigar a discriminação entre rostos reais e deepfake. O achado extraído é diretamente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Are you for real? Decoding realistic AI-generated faces from neural activity

judge.evidence_empirical: We investigated how the human brain encodes and interprets realistic artificially generated images using behaviour and brain imaging.
judge.evidence_topic: We investigated how the human brain encodes and interprets realistic artificially generated images using behaviour and brain imaging.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga como o cérebro humano codifica e interpreta rostos sintéticos realistas gerados por IA, usando dados próprios de comportamento e neuroimagem. O método extraído (decodificação neural e tarefa de classificação) é consistente com o resumo, e o achado principal está claramente apoiado no texto.

items.title: Cortical-striatal brain network distinguishes deepfake from real speaker identity

judge.evidence_empirical: During an identity matching task, participants show intermediate performance with deepfake voices, indicating levels of deception and resistance to deepfake identity spoofing.
judge.evidence_topic: test the neurocognitive sensitivity of 25 participants to accept or reject person identities as recreated in audio deepfakes
judge.reason: O artigo investiga a sensibilidade neurocognitiva a deepfakes de áudio, enquadrando-se no tema da percepção humana de mídia sintética. O estudo é empírico, com participantes realizando uma tarefa de correspondência de identidade enquanto os dados de fMRI são coletados. O método extraído (discriminação de vozes reais e deepfake durante fMRI) bate com o resumo. O achado principal é sustentado integralmente: o resumo afirma que os participantes tiveram desempenho intermédio e que uma rede cortical-estriatal distingue a identidade do falante deepfake da real.

items.title: Warning: Humans cannot reliably detect speech deepfakes

judge.evidence_empirical: We presented genuine and deepfake audio to n = 529 individuals and asked them to identify the deepfakes.
judge.evidence_topic: We presented genuine and deepfake audio to n = 529 individuals and asked them to identify the deepfakes.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga a capacidade humana de detectar deepfakes de fala, alinhando-se ao tema de percepção de mídia sintética. Trata-se de um experimento com dados próprios (529 participantes). O método extraído corresponde ao descrito no resumo. O achado extraído ('73% de identificação correta') é exatamente o dado do resumo.

items.title: People are poorly equipped to detect AI-powered voice clones

judge.evidence_topic: Through a series of perceptual studies, we report on the realism of AI-generated voices... We find human participants cannot consistently identify recordings of AI-generated voices.
judge.evidence_empirical: Through a series of perceptual studies... human participants...
judge.reason: O artigo trata da percepção humana de vozes sintéticas (clones de voz), enquadrando-se no tema e recorte do pedido. É um estudo empírico experimental com participantes humanos, conforme exigido. O tipo de estudo e o método extraídos coincidem com a descrição do resumo. O achado principal está literalmente respaldado pelo resumo. O tamanho da amostra não é informado no resumo, e a extração reflete isso corretamente.

items.title: Voice clones sound realistic but not (yet) hyperrealistic

judge.evidence_empirical: We find that voice clones can sound as real as human voices, making it difficult for listeners to distinguish between them.
judge.evidence_topic: We investigated the extent to which AI-generated voices sound real to human listeners, and whether listeners can accurately distinguish between human and AI-generated voices.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga a percepção humana de vozes geradas por IA (clones de voz), avaliando realismo e capacidade de distinção, o que se alinha ao tema do pedido. É um estudo empírico com ouvintes humanos, como evidenciado pelos resultados relatados. O tipo de estudo e método extraídos correspondem ao resumo. O achado principal, de que clones de voz soam tão reais quanto vozes humanas mas não são hiper-realistas, é diretamente sustentado pelo resumo.
